name: Look past the expected outline

uses.action: Compare the outline plate with known blocks, then turn the practice fitting and see which feature the first surface view hid.
Trace the patent under the narrow viewer and open the whole page to find the part of the application that the first frame kept out of sight.

name: Find out what a stamp vouches for

uses.action: Turn over the display seal and pair it with the source check before letting a public reader rely on the title.

name: Choose what readers can check without a specialist

uses.action: Bring the two watch readings and the independent rail record to the loading crew and set out a check they can repeat.
Keep the writing’s placeholder mark and the separately dated bark pieces in view while the guide preserves the limit raised by historians of mathematics.

name: Keep the facts available before the repair

uses.action: Keep the original drought order beside the repaired gate result so a reader can see the conditions Sena had when she made the first choice.

name: Leave a public trace of a changed mind

uses.action: After a listener says back the two proposals, sign a revised bench minute and leave the remaining request for someone to pick up.

name: Find the callers a desk cannot hear

uses.action: Keep Ade’s route rule fixed, replace desk-hours requests with the joined walking-round tally, and trace who the first window count left out.

name: Challenge a claim and keep the part that holds

uses.action: Bring Idris the museum entry with two makers, then acknowledge what the short tag can do on a delivery or keep both records on his strap.

name: Follow testimony back through its runners

uses.action: Fit Elian’s source clip and replay both runner orders. Follow the ridge keeper and bridge runner back to one ridge reading, then keep Fern’s creek slip on its own line.
Replay the council envelopes with their source marks visible. Match Sena’s forwarded check to Omi’s entry and keep the lower crew’s own reading.
Use Kunit’s recorded explanation and the report of his coast piece, then compare which changing relation the invented practice blocks let a second reader check.

name: Mark the blank the crew never checked

uses.action: Bring a visitor’s reading back to Sora and add where each survey stopped so a blank cannot pass for a finding.

name: See another reader’s position before rewriting

uses.action: Try the stairs and quay arrivals, find the marker the other route hides, and leave directions that start at the place each reader reaches.

name: Take responsibility for a missing check

uses.action: After seeing who the route board missed, mark the remaining service gaps and set a way for Lin to hear the next caller.

name: Check the cues an opaque sorter uses

uses.action: Pass the same four wrappers through the press by ink and by stamp, holding the packet fixed while its calls change.

name: Leave a record that can do part of the remembering

uses.action: Clip a source and short direction together, then compare what reached Kip with the independent docket after the relay.
Make a strip a new reader can follow to the exact object record, then try whether the receiving route can recover the source.

name: Find who a single distribution channel misses

uses.action: Put the approved excerpt at the rail or the staffed desk, then follow the chosen channel to see which check its reader can reach.

name: Keep a busy tally separate from its cause

uses.action: Run the same rule on desk requests and walking-round requests. A bigger number can come from whom the crew found, without a change in the local need.

name: Check whether words lead different readers to different places

uses.action: Carry one ferry slip from the road and from the dock stair, recording which landmark each group starts from even when the bundle is the same.

name: Open a strong heading to see what it passes over

uses.action: Lay the polished cut beside its old notice and job slip. Put the omitted time and trial conditions back beside the short wording.

name: Carry a local meaning across a language boundary

uses.action: Lay the shortened invitation by the visitor’s scrap and examine how velin names both the menders’ care for the bench and a place anyone can share.
Fit the ferry phrase to the council slate, then use the back-check to keep the cart, pace, time and shared-work meanings before sending it.

name: Make a permission real by issuing it

uses.action: Give Sena the signed appeal and local check, then authorize a particular receiving run so the service gate opens for that delivery.
Sign the goods voucher to reserve stock at Oduya’s shelf or sign credit that Corvan’s counter can spend against its dated quote.

name: See who gets the first version and what they can act on

uses.action: Check the household purse before putting one version of the basket comparison in front of its first readers.

name: Decide who the official tally counts

uses.action: Run one allocation rule on the desk-only tally and again with the walking crew’s slips joined in. Check the desk heading against both results before publishing windows.

name: Keep an objection available without exposing a claimant

uses.action: Use the permit gate to make the second handover. Leave the public count and time available while Ade keeps the claimants’ names and requests under seal.

name: Let the trials change the public order

uses.action: Keep the signed drought order on the register, and use the repeated setting and repaired run to make a new order suited to the changed gate.

name: Build a check other people can repeat

uses.action: Align the archive source with the press and landing copies and show Lark where time and source were lost before the correction goes out.
Build a packet across the workshop roles, carry the call and compare the reply against the signed docket before letting either stand for the whole handover.

name: Check how someone can repeat a spoken route

uses.action: Read the account of Kunit explaining his particular coast and island pieces, then turn the practice block with the island peg held fixed and give the next reader a repeatable starting mark.

name: Carry permission with the public excerpt

uses.action: Set the approved passage at the visiting bench or reading slot, and keep the second band and its signed index for the authorised hearing.
Read the permission slip and place the approved extract on the rail or at the source desk while the private note stays in its sleeve.

name: Check whether a steady reading measures the job

uses.action: Run the upper ferry and a second route with the same crate count. Keep the exact number of marked-strip crossings apart from what the model can say about sound.
Line up the empty and tabbed reference blocks, then rotate one fitting so the team can tell which steady marks locate the hidden tab and which trace only the outside.
Move the registration stops, then compare the watched dot with the control in both exposures before leaving an orientation guide or a dated watch slot.

name: Check an exact-looking time against its reference

uses.action: Advance the three tests on the workshop watch. Compare the same minute display to its independent time reference before deciding how to use that reading.
Move the precise year peg across two different ranges, then give the reader both labelled ranges so the exact year does not turn into a making date.
Find where both catalogue ranges admit the same year, then keep the two object dates separate when you prepare the public guide.

name: Keep the interaction a single gauge misses

uses.action: Open two inlet setups and clip basin, return and spill readings for each before sending a design on.

name: Use a model with its limit still on the board

uses.action: Keep the usable upper-landing route, then change the dock sheet for the lower berth after testing the changed ramp.

name: Check a confident speaker’s particular claim

uses.action: Use the guild ledger and Hesper’s sheet against Corvan’s supplier story about an ancient blade, then defend the part the dated records actually establish.

name: Keep the full chain when a copied line returns

uses.action: Put the corrected trial proof beside the landing sheet and check that the source and time return together.

name: Keep the unmet turn when choosing a workable one

uses.action: Write an actual staffing or turn rule after the two bench tests, and carry the request it still leaves waiting on the signed minute.

name: Find the one case that breaks an all-rule

uses.action: Keep Idris’s one-name tag and fetch the museum and patent-office account that credits more than one maker of that same pen.

name: Test what changes when one starting rule changes

uses.action: Keep three moves, the two Oak-bank endpoints and the no-repeat rule fixed. Trace both branches first with crossings alone, then with one named same-bank link. The added link admits two paths in the same move limit.

name: Compare a short general proof with a checked list

uses.action: Fold three bank marks to rule out every all-crossing trail at once. Then unfold both actual branches and see which assumption makes the short proof work and where its conclusion stops applying.

name: Let the marks show which pieces make a whole

uses.action: Try grouping the same inserts before wrapping or after bundling, then set a tag the next handler can use to recover the parts.
Slide a spare mark between two digits to keep a place visible, then put that demonstration with a dated source reference at the chosen receiver.

name: Update a route choice after seeing how a report was made

uses.action: Replay keeping and changing the cart route after a blocked gate is shown by each scout. Compare the different ledgers before using the reveal to shift your choice.

name: Change one support and repeat the first setting

uses.action: Run the first gate position again with the repaired gate before trying another position, so the recorded difference can be tied to the repair.
Match the control dot in both paper exposure models. Keep the growing watched dot tied to the changed exposure before opening a slot for a real series.

name: Make the readings distinguish two possible causes

uses.action: Advance all three watch cases and compare the advancing hand with a changing shadow and a separate rail cue.

name: Check an odd result against a new observation

uses.action: Return to both lookout places and preserve which view was obstructed before changing the forest’s public record.

name: Check what a stand-in measure actually tells you

uses.action: Walk to the margin worker’s report of a rattle at one bend and check what that place-and-time note adds to a route model that counts quiet-strip crossings.

name: Keep each specialist’s part of a shared check

uses.action: Share the evidence jobs across Hesper, Sefa and Kip, and check the transferred instruction using Rook’s independent docket.
Keep Jane Goodall’s observation and the later record crediting Baraka Daniel on separate evidence lines so the two contributions survive the handoff.

name: Keep a recovered observation distinct from a model trial

uses.action: Read the exact Pitons algal record, then test the model shore grid at a fixed spot over time or at two spots on one bell. Give the model check its own conditions.

name: Check how a local observer’s reading can join the record

uses.action: Visit the upper peg, find the lower crew’s own reading and keep a location and time with each before sharing the comparison.

name: Check what a label counts

uses.action: Compare the early hook tally with the complete-kit count to see how a chosen record turns a partly done job into a reported success.

name: See how the target moves the work

uses.action: Post the early tag target and trace the split hooks and later feet. Change the target to matched kits, check the two later grouped arrivals, and fit the same four parts before comparing the public tallies.

name: Keep the performed movement and the audience’s reading separate

uses.action: Ask what the audience took from the pause and leave that reading in the program alongside the rehearsal record for the movement.

name: Test what a survey question does to the answer

uses.action: Run Venn’s bridge survey with the same outreach group and different wording, then compare the meeting and house samples before sending the report.

name: Give missing voices a visible place in the archive

uses.action: Set Carter’s named foremen, workers’ photographs and the missing workers’ own written accounts on the excavation side. Give the current trainee’s name request a separate tray.

name: Keep dated grounds for changing the public record

uses.action: Bring the excavation file and later note to the proof sheet, then leave a traceable lead with the uncertainty the records still leave.

name: Try the changed condition before telling the story

uses.action: Compare what a moving hand, stopped hand and changing shutter each produce on the watch model. A plausible alternative should make a repeatable difference.

name: Check a written account against an object

uses.action: Check the marks on the surviving Singapore Stone fragment and the written account of Badang’s rock. Leave the association as its own claim when you assemble the return-table label.
Fit the gauge notch at the Cold Store jig, match its stamped number to the tool list, then check whether the gift book settles the owner line.

name: Keep one broad period label from swallowing two dates

uses.action: Move the date ribbon to show both the named event and the span it can actually bound, then check what a visitor can recover.
Use the dated catalogue and print at the case, then keep the 1865–66 photographic view and the later print date beside the working sheet.

name: Check both the shape on view and its making record

uses.action: Use two lights on the unchanged relief, trace the different visible marks, and open the maker’s separate dated slip.

name: Rehearse an arrival from another group’s place

uses.action: Try the same welcome from the road and the bench before arranging the real festival cue. Find who misses the stop when you change position.

name: Give the performed cue and the printed copy separate jobs

uses.action: Use rehearsal and the audience’s response, then keep the performed pause and its public reading distinct on the program.

name: Choose which record visitors encounter first

uses.action: Open with the temple and reign or with the known burial and custody trail. Watch the visitor’s first question change and keep the other dated source reachable.

name: Check what a warning means in this batch

uses.action: Run the same warning die on both practice racks and compare how many of the marked parcels actually needed a seal. The repairs start out rarer on one rack.

name: Find the parcel rather than guess from its group

uses.action: Follow Orla to the receiving desk and match wet Ash parcel W-2 to its own signed arrival. The wet Ash count records one success and one late box without identifying either.

name: Slide the loads apart to see why the lead changes

uses.action: Use the wet shutter and bright shutter separately, then pull up both on the same board. Compare the reversal and which label carried mostly bright loads.

name: Follow a current description to the record it describes

uses.action: Line up the archive source with the printed and carried versions, then show Lark where an access copy lost a source line.
Bring the folio to the treaty and the accounts of Tecumseh’s challenge; keep the names and periods each source records before choosing what to open first.

name: Find the evidence left by work done for a different purpose

uses.action: Use the stone’s visible trace alongside the account of the transfer and put the two kinds of support on the notice.

name: Look for people a survey route misses

uses.action: Collect the public desk and walking-crew slips from different stops before counting them. Compare who could file at the desk and which requests arrived outside it.
Compare the bridge meeting’s responses with responses collected from houses using the same plain question.

name: Keep a hidden view from passing for a scattered count

uses.action: Repeat the two watches, check the return view and note the obstruction separately before passing on a comparison.

name: Compare a bunched-up tray with its chance baseline

uses.action: Group the possible arrival marks for the dispatch trays and read when the workshop releases its crews. Check whether shared marks reflect chance or a scheduled handover.

name: Check a frame’s place and date before using it

uses.action: Record the three beats from the front and the wing and file each frame with its camera position before using the cut to guide a visitor.
Compare the dated older still with the painted post on the ground and the carrier’s current direction. Keep the picture’s place evidence separate from today’s instruction.

name: Retest a working setup under local conditions

uses.action: Fit the Archive strip or the Island card and collect three readings under Ivo’s smaller inlet and higher power demand. Check whether the old setup can still power the plate.
Fit Corra’s chosen teaching guide at the receiving bench and see whether the trainee can trace the outer edge or locate the tab with that view.

name: Find an object first and earn the link later

uses.action: Start with a found gauge, then use the jig and trace its number to the gift file before making a claim about its owner.

name: Keep missing knowledge separate from a missing thing

uses.action: Put the survey boundary beside an unmarked stretch rather than letting white paper stand for clear water.

name: Separate what is measured from what a rule makes official

uses.action: Collect the named goods under Oduya’s voucher or fit a different basket to Corvan’s credit. Check the counted goods against the convention that gives each paper its right.
Use the carrier’s permission card and the signed entry to date the actual trial crossing and the later public opening separately.

name: Give readers a route to check a keeper’s account

uses.action: Carry the approved notice to the chosen working stand and let the reader recover its source or the checked directions from there.

name: Count independent checks in a chain of reports

uses.action: Move the source clip through two runner orders so Omi’s record and its forwarded copy cannot masquerade as two independent readings.

name: Test what one service word allows different crews to do

uses.action: Check the menders’ tagged row and the lookout’s gauge before putting both uses of clear where the relevant crews can find them.

name: Try how a change to the rule changes the result

uses.action: Keep the joined request tally and run it under two service rules to preview who would reach each window.

name: Keep a useful record of what the check could not show

uses.action: Return to both lookouts and leave the screened view marked as obstructed. Keep that observation separate from an open watch with no sighting.
Try the custody-first card and trace the known burial and cache locations. Leave the move date open for the reader who uses that trail.

name: Check what a matching cue really proves

uses.action: Watch for the stopped mechanism whose mark still lines up once, then advance the trial and check the independent rail record.

name: Keep a copied agreement separate from an independent one

uses.action: Set the original, forwarded copy and lower crew’s own check in different slots while replaying both delivery orders.

name: Find which part of a record needs checking

uses.action: Use the Lens on the excavation journal and later note. Keep the first report and later intervention as distinct jobs for the evidence.

name: Translate an instrument trace for the next person doing the work

uses.action: Fit the teaching guide to the receiving bench and see what the new trainee can reproduce with the surface and hidden-edge checks.

name: Give forecast confidence its own time boundary

uses.action: Go back at the next bell, use the new headland reading and leave the older notice alongside its updated conditions.

name: Keep the whole flow visible behind the local numbers

uses.action: Switch inlet setups and compare the pool, return path and spill as a connected trial, so an improvement at one dial cannot stand for the whole loop.

name: Use different words for a memory and a signed opening

uses.action: Put the carrier’s remembered walk and the clerk’s signed public opening on separate dated lines.

name: Keep the other side’s good reason in a changed notice

uses.action: Change the signed bench rule after hearing both cases, and use its second line to preserve the waiting job the chosen rule cannot do.

name: Give the reader a route from each claim to its grounds

uses.action: Set the evidence strip where the reader can follow the claim back to the particular record, and check the path they take.

name: Give each version one job it can do

uses.action: Run the signed landing record through a walking brief and a separate desk brief. Keep the direction in one and the way to find the check in the other.

name: Make the effect of a chosen rule clear in its public wording

uses.action: Mark the actual gap after checking the reader’s reply, then give the future notice a specific time or review route.

name: Post the place and conditions where a claim applies

uses.action: Name where the shore walk ended and where the shoal survey stopped, then keep both limits on the directions readers use.
Keep the drought order legible and add a separate repaired-gate order. Limit the later claim to the gate and work cards checked under repair.
Turn two kinds of exhibit strip and move each berth name to the row for its own trial, or clip a per-circuit tab to each count. Read the copy made by the chosen edit.
Make a working sight line for the Xiamen harbour entrance and keep the limit that a visible opening cannot establish water depth.

name: Keep the job of a label stable across two receipts

uses.action: Try the short spoken call, then place the same collection prefixes in the Council receipt so two nearby numbers keep their different owners.

name: Name which person made each check

uses.action: Trace the two credited contributions separately in the Gombe records before adding the named source roles to the account.

name: Replace a question mark with a record that someone can check

uses.action: Follow the lamp to Dagny’s desk, match it to the earlier pickup and record what part of the handback actually happened.

name: Keep the compared conditions explicit in a short notice

uses.action: Give both the drought order and the repaired-gate decision enough room to keep the conditions with each line.

name: Find the record for a particular machine

uses.action: Use the source check for CERN’s exact NeXT computer to set a workable landing copy, preserving enough identifiers for the next reader to find that computer.

name: Keep the named object recoverable in its working caption

uses.action: Make a record of where the sight line opened or the second observer stood and keep the accession for Le Gray’s two-negative print with it.

name: Make a specific object do a job in the route

uses.action: Use Watkins’s exact later print to make a repeatable line of sight, keeping the separate negative and print dates with the result.

name: Follow what a reader actually does with the notice

uses.action: Follow the reader who took the trial’s return-slip line as an admission rule. Rewrite the trial result and the hall’s entry rule on separate lines.
Screen both cuts and post one. Find how the visitor used its door or hand cue and identify the frame they had to go back for.
Check Nellin’s installed bay to see whether its copy prompted a crew to split a load or helped a visitor trace the tally. Bring that bay’s own notice back to Quiet Margin.

name: Check what fails when two exact sources are swapped

uses.action: Open the two exact collection records separately and check why the same shortened accession can point to two separate cases.

name: See what a permission slip puts on the official record

uses.action: Place the holder’s trial permission beside the public register. Use each document to state who could cross at its own dated turn.
Fit the previously prepared folio to the separate Wea convention and the Eastern Shawnee Tribe of Oklahoma’s constitution. Check the date and named authority on each source.

name: Find the feature a tool turns into a reading

uses.action: Make the surface trace, compare the known blocks under the plate, and turn the same fitting to locate a feature the outline left unmeasured.
Read the upper peg with the notebook open. Move to the clear lower viewpoint or keep the lower crew’s earlier handover with its own time and leave noon open.

name: Walk to the edge a guide leaves out

uses.action: Read the harbour chart and shoal survey after a visitor takes the blank as safe ground. Mark where each survey stopped so the blank keeps its own coverage.
Try the same room sketch from the shelf end and the aisle. Follow where its turning marks work from each approach.

name: Keep a found thing’s context with its identification

uses.action: Return with the Cold Store receipt and link it to the exact gauge entry before the keeper closes the found record.

name: Keep the picture tied to one named object

uses.action: Compare the side and overhead pictures of the same jar. Fit a two-view mount that lets a reader find both views under one exact accession.

name: Commit a workable plan and retain its cost

uses.action: Use an actual tested relief branch and walk to the installed outlet. Leave the other crew’s pending need visible with the choice.

name: Test what a source can support before using it in an inquiry

uses.action: Use the Lens to compare the dates of the three pen records and separate what each date can support before preparing the source case.

name: Follow a service decision to the person who uses it

uses.action: Place the tested ramp where one group can use it and travel to that stop to see how the new queue works for its readers.

name: Check how what remains limits a historical account

uses.action: Place an old acknowledgment apart from a new receiving roster, and see which part of the handling each can trace.

name: Separate an experiment’s readout from the target in service

uses.action: Fit a starting card to the new Island inlet, then compare the fresh basin, return and spill readings before fitting anything permanently.
Scale the watched mark to the control on each model exposure before leaving a chart or a dated watch slot. A brighter-looking dot does not establish a brightness cycle.

name: Give a reader both the source words and their practical meaning

uses.action: Try guide copies for different approaches and keep what each word tells that reader about reaching the marked place.

name: Use a grouping rule a second person can reconstruct

uses.action: Arrange the same dispatch pieces in different grouping orders, then test whether the recipient can recover the individual amounts from the resulting tag.
Balance square areas in two frame lengths, then supply a checked guide whose method another runner can repeat.

name: Take both positions and invite a listener to join them

uses.action: Move between stands, make both cases and listen as someone working at the bench restates what each would mean for them.

name: Keep a model answer tied to the particular check it can pass

uses.action: Unseal the records from both sites and compare their actual handovers with the printed calls before claiming the rule has travelled.

name: Link a claim to its connected records

uses.action: Follow the blade’s provenance thread from the stall to the guild ledger and the workshop, so three distinct records can answer different parts of the same claim.

name: Make the strongest alternative visible before committing

uses.action: Put the evidence for the competing plan on its own stand, then invite the waiting reader to test the strongest version of each proposal.

name: Move from a visible clue to a repeatable check

uses.action: Use the low eye notch, ask where the hidden pavilion edge appears, then move the screen or go around the end to let Merrit repeat the check.

name: Run a source check before sending the copy

uses.action: Place the corrected proof where a reader can recover the exact painting and catalogue, then see which part of the promised route they can actually follow.

name: Use a new check on an object you first trusted

uses.action: Bring Lia a way to check the first pen exhibit, visit the person who uses it and follow the resulting note back to the opening stand.
